### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **35** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**54** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 295699d51d1484a735989450238ec2e14c0c1104`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 36 pages)`
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **56** of **208** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **148** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 295699d51d1484a735989450238ec2e14c0c1104` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `959ac8483df2eeb637151e79babcf1d71835dd7c` — the merge of head `897e8d89aff69b18cc77197d807f4cd03cda4d73` into base `295699d51d1484a735989450238ec2e14c0c1104`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 959ac8483df2eeb637151e79babcf1d71835dd7c && git checkout 959ac8483df2eeb637151e79babcf1d71835dd7c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 295699d51d1484a735989450238ec2e14c0c1104 897e8d89aff69b18cc77197d807f4cd03cda4d73 && git checkout -B drift-repro 295699d51d1484a735989450238ec2e14c0c1104 && git merge --no-ff 897e8d89aff69b18cc77197d807f4cd03cda4d73

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 295699d51d1484a735989450238ec2e14c0c1104
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 295699d51d1484a735989450238ec2e14c0c1104` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d53bd33122bdf502502bb782de3a75ef46b8360b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md, skills/objectstack-ui/SKILL.md + ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/deriveRelatedLists.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/__tests__/deriveRelatedLists.relatedListsOrder-27069.test.ts, packages/spec/src/stack-related-lists-order.test.ts, ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/synth/buildDefaultPageSchema.ts (`buildDefaultTabs`), ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx (:1848, :3256-3299), packages/lint/src/validate-semantic-roles.ts (rules (a)/(b)/(d)), packages/lint/src/object-field-groups.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-object-field-refs.ts, docs/adr/0035-config-driven-master-detail.md (:84-96), docs/adr/0085-object-semantic-roles-over-surface-hint-blocks.md (§2), .changeset/27069-related-lists-order.md, packages/spec/liveness/object.json + field.json, packages/spec/src/compose-stacks-*.test.ts (the two pins), examples/app-crm/src/objects/opportunity-line-item.object.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/invoice.object.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/expense-report.object.ts, packages/metadata and packages/objectql hotcrm `__fixtures__` (census only). The remainder of the diff (generated docs, authorable-surface baseline, platform-objects translation bundles and their two pins, the metadata-protocol count pin) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Inputs read: card #27069 body and its two comments (claim 6465054400, os-dev-report 6467128510); epic #26676 round-3 comments 6459899198 and 6460478339; PR #27215 body, file list (27 files) and the net diff against the merge base `4265176cf3` (origin/main at `9dacccf961`); the 41 check-runs on the head.

Check-runs on `d53bd3312` at read time (2026-10-28), 41 in all: 11 completed success (Spec property liveness, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected, Auto Label, Plan Test Core shards, filter), 7 skipped (opt-in / schedule gates), 23 in progress (Type Check x4, Test Core 1-8/8, Lint x8, Build Core / Build UI Deps / Build Docs). No red at read time; the in-progress families are reported as counts, not verdicts.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged against the tree:

1. `ObjectSchema.relatedLists?: string[]`, each entry `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*)?$` — RIGHT. The grammar is the object/field machine-name grammar with at most one dot, judged at parse with no new refinement node; `relatedLists: 'task'`, `[1]`, `['Task']`, `['a.b.c']` are refused by the shape (pinned in `stack-related-lists-order.test.ts`). Sits beside `highlightFields`, as the card asked. `objectExtensions` cannot contribute it (`ObjectExtensionSchema` is strict with no such key), the same as `highlightFields`.
2. `ObjectFieldGroupSchema.relatedList?: string`, same grammar — RIGHT in shape. The group schema carries no `fields` key (membership is `Field.group` → `fieldGroups[].key`), so "a group with relatedList carries no fields" is realised as `refuseFieldsInRelatedListGroups`: one located issue at `['fields', NAME, 'group']` per field naming such a group, inside the object's existing `superRefine`, so the JSON Schema projection drops nothing new. Judged against the lint gate it must co-exist with, it does NOT hold today — see ④ M2.
3. `defineStack` refuses a `relatedLists` entry or a group `relatedList` that matches no inbound `lookup`/`master_detail` field, `STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID` with `code` + numeric `status`, the message naming the entry and the inbound relationships spelled as an entry may name them (`'rlo_task', 'rlo_event.who_id', 'rlo_event.related_to'`, or `it has none`) — RIGHT, and placed where `highlightFields`' sibling cross-object checks sit (`validateCrossReferences`, after `collectHydratedInlineColumnErrors`). The walk covers `config.objects`, every `packages[].manifest.objects` (the assembled `ArtifactPackageSchema` body does carry object definitions there; the same pattern `applyControlledByParentExtensionGate` uses) and the fields `objectExtensions` add. Audit FKs (`created_by`/`updated_by`/`owner_id`) are excluded by field name, matching the reader's `AUDIT_FK_FIELDS`. Artifact-scoped: a child named only by a sibling package (`artifactObjects`) or a platform-prefixed object is left unjudged ONLY when the child is nowhere in `fieldsByObject`; a declared child with no such FK is refused. Consistent with the #18202 ARTIFACT-SCOPED classes. Two limits, graded should-fix in ④ (S3): the check sits below `if (objectNames.size === 0) return errors;`, so an artifact-only definition (objects only in package bodies) never reaches it, contrary to the docblock; and `seen` keys by object identity, so a name declared both top-level and in a body is judged twice.
4. `relatedList: 'primary'` re-read as placement, no longer ordering — RIGHT per the card's target 2 ("its meaning becomes PLACEMENT"). `resolveRelatedListOrder` is the one resolution: listed first in declared order (a list takes the position of the FIRST entry naming it; a bare child name takes every list of that child in their derived order; `object.field` takes one), unlisted after in today's derived order (owned then lookup, discovery order). `relatedList: false` still hides a listed relationship (the FK is skipped before the list exists, so the entry places nothing). An unknown entry places nothing. `buildDefaultTabs` is unchanged and filters `isPrimary` into own tabs and the rest into the Related tab, preserving order within each half, so the card's acceptance 2 holds on the tabbed page: `['task', 'campaign_member']` renders tasks, campaign members, then the rest; `primary` still promotes an unlisted list (own tab) without moving its order. All pinned in the 11-case app-shell test.
5. An absent `relatedList` on a `master_detail` FK that sets `inlineEdit` (`true` / `'grid'` / `'form'`, the three arms `FieldSchema.inlineEdit` declares) is `isPrimary` by default; explicit `true` opts out; `lookup` + `inlineEdit` does not default — RIGHT per the maintainer's line-items ruling quoted in the card (「明细行的子表放在右侧合适嘛？」 → the body). Only one branch on the value exists under `ui/` (`deriveRelatedLists.ts`; `RecordDetailView` forwards `isPrimary`, `buildDefaultTabs` splits on it; no second derivation under `ui/apps`), and `MetadataProvider` passes object keys through, so `objectDef.relatedLists` reaches the reader.
6. Census of what visibly moves on today's tabbed page from the default in 5 (whole head tree, non-test code): THREE in-repo parents — `crm_opportunity` (examples/app-crm, `crm_opportunity_line_item.opportunity`: `inlineEdit: 'grid'`, no `relatedList`), `showcase_invoice` (`showcase_invoice_line.invoice`, same) and `showcase_expense_report` (`showcase_expense_line.expense_report`, same). Each gains its own "Products" / "Line Items" / "Expense Lines" tab and leaves the shared Related tab on merge. `packages/platform-objects`: no `inlineEdit` FK at all, nothing moves. The three hotcrm fixtures in repo (`packages/metadata/src/__fixtures__/hotcrm-17.1-*`, `packages/objectql/src/__fixtures__/hotcrm-4.0.1-*`) carry no `inlineEdit` and no `relatedList`, nothing moves. `Field.masterDetail` sets no `relatedList` default, so the builder path is the raw path. No test or e2e pins the Related tab for those three parents, so the move is silent in CI — which is exactly why the changeset should name them (④ S2).
7. Compose: `relatedLists` joins the derived object collection-key list, so two declarations of one object both carrying it are refused at merge, as `highlightFields` is — RIGHT (the two compose pins move by one row each). A relationship contributed by another package is seen by the check only when both halves are in one `defineStack` call (composed stacks, or an artifact's package bodies); a package validated alone with a parent naming a sibling's child relies on `artifactObjects`, exactly as the other artifact-scoped classes do.
8. Studio: `object.form.ts` gains the `relatedLists` string-tags row after `highlightFields` and a `relatedList` text sub-row in the `fieldGroups` repeater; labels and help in four locales (platform-objects, lane remainder) — RIGHT. The help text honestly states the publish-door gap ("os validate refuses it"), which is true: `os validate` imports the stack, so `defineStack`'s throw is the refusal.
9. `FieldSchema.relatedList` TSDoc/describe re-read — RIGHT against the reader; the tabbed-page parenthetical keeps today's behaviour visible.
10. Liveness: `object.relatedLists` is `live` with the reader (`resolveRelatedListOrder`, `deriveRelatedLists` → `RecordDetailView`) and the authoring judge named; `field.relatedList` / `relatedListTitle` re-cited. The deriveRelatedLists citations (:367, :378-379) are exact on the head; the `RecordDetailView.tsx:1827` citation is :1848 on the merge head (the pre-merge line; `Spec property liveness` is green, observation only). `fieldGroups[].relatedList` has no row and shelters under `object/fieldGroups` = `live` by a dogfood proof that never exercises `relatedList` — graded in ④ S4.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` — RIGHT. Two new optional keys; the only new refusals (`fields.X.group` naming a relatedList group; a dangling relatedList name at `defineStack`) bite only input that could not exist before this head, so nothing previously accepted is refused.

`Metadata-protocol: semantic` — RIGHT, and the dev's step-3 upgrade from the card's `added` is the correct reading under AGENTS.md step 3 ("a changed meaning or default is `semantic`; several ⇒ narrowed over semantic over added"): `'primary'` changes meaning (order → placement) and the absent value changes default on an inline-edited `master_detail` FK. Both declaration lines are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset body.

Changeset `.changeset/27069-related-lists-order.md`: `@objectstack/spec` minor (the kind takes at least minor), `@object-ui/app-shell` minor (the reader's behaviour moves without a metadata edit), `@objectstack/platform-objects` minor (the generated metadata-form bundles move), `@objectstack/skills` minor (a package 13 other changesets in the root `.changeset` already name) — all RIGHT. It is in the root `.changeset`, carries both declaration lines and a "What to do" migration note for the semantic default (`relatedList: true` keeps the old placement), which is what step 3 asks of a semantic change (the mandatory FROM → TO mapping is the breaking-only clause). `Check Changeset` is green on the head. One should-fix on the note's content, ④ S2: it does not census the movers.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions: []` — nothing to answer. The three `out_of_scope_findings` and the four PR acceptance notes:

- Publish-door gap (dev flag 1, seat ask (a)): CONFIRMED on this head. `runtimeAuthoringRulesFor('object')` dispatches no rule that reads `relatedLists` or `fieldGroups[].relatedList`; `validate-object-field-refs.ts` is same-object by design and `validateSemanticRoles` is fenced off that door (#4716). A Studio / REST `/meta` / MCP save of `relatedLists: ['nope']` is accepted and the reader places nothing. The form's help text says so. Recorded as ④ S3 for the delta review; the carrier the dev names (seat 1 / lint lane) is right, but the rule belongs in this card's delta, not a new card, because the key ships here.
- `fieldGroups[].relatedList` ahead of its renderer (dev flag 2, seat ask (b)): CONFIRMED. No reader on the head (`git grep relatedList` under `ui/` branches only in `deriveRelatedLists.ts`, on the FK flag, never on a group). The key is `live` by inheritance from the `object/fieldGroups` container whose proof is the semantic-roles dogfood. Recorded as ④ S4: a row of its own at `planned`, carrier #27055.
- ADR-0035's read-side table (dev flag 3): the dev defers the amended status line to #27055 because "'primary' promotes it to its own tab" stays true on the tabbed page. ESCALATED to a must-fix (④ M1): the sentence this head falsifies is not that one but the DEFAULT sentence on the same page — "`true` / omitted shows the child under a single shared Related tab" — and "a prominence hint, not a layout switch". Both are reversed on this head, not on #27055's.
- Bare child name with several FKs orders all of that child's lists rather than being refused as ambiguous (acceptance note 4): ACCEPTED. The card's grammar says `object.field` is for the multi-FK case and never says a bare name is then refused; the dev's reading is the less surprising one and the refusal message spells the per-FK names for such a child, so an author who wants one list is told how.
- Reader drag order (#27055/#27052) and HotCRM declarations (hotcrm follow-up): out of this card, correctly left.
- ADR-0085 §2 admission: `relatedLists` passes test 1 (business importance is not inferable) and test 2 (no page name; it binds the object's relationships across surfaces, the `highlightFields` precedent); `fieldGroups[].relatedList` is a layout-role entry under ADR-0085 §5 exactly as `fieldGroups` already is, and the maintainer ruled the placement (「他如果做到放在基本信息下面」). No contradiction with ADR-0085's text; the re-reading of `'primary'` from "prominence" to "placement" should be noted beside ADR-0035's amendment (M1) since the old TSDoc cited prominence as the admission argument.

### ④ Design judgment

**packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts** — against ruling A and its first consumer (`deriveRelatedLists`). `relatedLists`: holds. Grammar, describe, placement beside `highlightFields`, extension-proof, compose-key: all as the card asks, and the reader resolves exactly what the describe promises. `ObjectFieldGroupSchema.relatedList` + `refuseFieldsInRelatedListGroups`: the parse-time half holds (correct path, message names the group and the list), but the design does not hold against the lint gate the same object passes through:

- **M2 (must-fix)**: `packages/lint/src/validate-semantic-roles.ts` rule (b) `FIELD_GROUP_EMPTY` fires on every group that carries `relatedList` — "fieldGroups declares 'lines' but no field references it — the group never renders. Assign at least one field via group: 'lines', or remove the unused group declaration." — and that hint prescribes the one thing this head refuses at `fields.X.group`. The card's own example (`{ name: 'lines', label: '报价明细', relatedList: 'crm_quote_line_item.crm_quote' }`) run through `os validate` / `os lint` is told to undo itself. A rule and the gate it must co-exist with are one change: exempt a group carrying `relatedList` from rule (b) (and from (d), which already skips empty groups) in this PR, with a pin. Warning-tier and CLI-only, but a contract that contradicts its own gate on the authoring path the help text points to is not a cosmetic miss.

**packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts** — `collectRelatedListNameErrors` against the ADR-0112 envelope and compose. Holds for the scenarios the card names (entry / `object.field` / unknown child / known child without FK / unknown field / no inbound at all / extension-added FK / sibling package / group relatedList), all pinned with `code` + numeric `status` + named subjects, never a bare `toThrow()`.

- **S3 (should-fix)**: the call sits below `if (objectNames.size === 0) return errors;`, so the package-body walk the docblock promises ("the stack's objects, every packages[].manifest.objects") never runs for a definition whose objects live only in package bodies. Either state that limit in the docblock (it is shared with every sibling check below that line) or hoist the call above it, since this check needs no top-level object to resolve against. Also, `seen` is keyed by record identity and dedupes nothing: a name declared both top-level and in a body is judged twice with merged fields, two identical issues. Minor; one line each.
- **S3' (should-fix, the seat's ask (a))**: the publish door. Add a `relatedLists` / `fieldGroups[].relatedList` dangling-name rule beside `validate-object-field-refs` at the tier that door dispatches, reading the registry the door has (the lint `object-graph` index, as `object-field-groups.ts` does), so a one-object save of `relatedLists: ['nope']` is refused rather than silently placing nothing. Until it lands the form help text's "os validate refuses it" is the only door.

**packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts** — the `relatedList` TSDoc and describe against the reader: holds. Every sentence has a line in `isMainContentList` / `buildDefaultTabs`. The three `inlineEdit` arms the default keys on are the three the schema declares.

- **M1 (must-fix)**: docs/adr/0035-config-driven-master-detail.md (Accepted) records, in its read-side table and the paragraph under it (:86-93): "`true` / omitted shows the child under a single shared Related tab; `'primary'` promotes the relationship to its own tab" and "`relatedList` is tri-state (a prominence hint, not a layout switch — see ADR-0085)". This head makes an omitted `relatedList` on an inline-edited `master_detail` FK — the exact relationship ADR-0035 is about — land in its own tab, and re-reads `'primary'` as placement. Prime Directive 13: reversing a recorded decision "needs a new ADR (or an amended status line on the old one), not a changeset that quietly does the opposite." The ruling is in hand (quoted in the card, 2026-10-28), so the fix is an amended status line on ADR-0035 citing #27069 and that ruling, with a one-line note on the two sentences it changes; add the same note to ADR-0085 §2 for the prominence → placement reading since the old TSDoc cited prominence as the key's admission argument. `docs/adr/**` is Tier H, and the PR already carries Tier H through `skills/**`, so it changes nothing about the landing path. The dev's deferral to #27055 is wrong on the facts: #27055 changes WHERE a primary list is drawn; this head changes WHICH lists are primary.

**packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts** — against Studio's form renderer and the spec: holds. Both rows match the key shapes (string-tags for `string[]`, text for the group's `string`), sit where the card asked, and the help texts say what the tree does, gap included.

**skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md** — against the spec on this head and the card's acceptance scenario: the tri-state bullets and the `relatedLists` bullet are accurate and the file is net smaller (ratchet green per the dev; CI's ratchet job in progress at read time).

- **S1 (should-fix)**: the bullet "`true` / omitted — a side card (the shared Related tab)" is contradicted one bullet up for the inline-edit default; say "`true`, or omitted on anything but an inline-edited `master_detail` — a side card". Same file, the code comment "read side: a body table (default with inlineEdit)" is right.

**skills/objectstack-ui/SKILL.md** — the `relatedList: 'primary'` bullet is accurate. But the "Related-list layout" paragraph that follows it (:117-128), untouched by the diff, still closes with "For arrangements the relationship layer can't express — filtered splits, a chart/report tab, **exact tab ordering** — assign the object a custom record Page". After this head exact tab ordering IS expressible: `relatedLists` orders the own tabs among themselves and the Related tab's lists among themselves (`buildDefaultTabs` preserves the resolved order within each half).

- **S1' (should-fix)**: drop "exact tab ordering" from that list (or point it at `relatedLists`), in the same file so the skill does not teach a custom Page for what the object key now does. Paid for by the line it removes.

**Cross-cutting**

- **S2 (should-fix)**: the changeset's "What to do" note is generic. Name the three in-repo parents whose record page visibly changes on merge (`crm_opportunity`, `showcase_invoice`, `showcase_expense_report` each gain an own line-items tab) so an upgrader greps a concrete symbol; the PR body should carry the same census under "Risk". Nothing in CI pins those tabs, so the changeset is the only place the move is visible.
- **S4 (should-fix, the seat's ask (b))**: give `fieldGroups[].relatedList` a liveness row of its own at `planned` (reader #27055), instead of inheriting `live` from the `object/fieldGroups` container whose dogfood proof never exercises it; the `object.relatedLists` note already names the reader, so the row is a move of that sentence.
- Observations, not graded (non-hits, non-reviewed): `buildDefaultPageSchema.ts:1003` "Owned-before-lookup order is preserved by deriveRelatedLists upstream" and the `isPrimary` TSDoc at :241-247 ("a CORE relationship") read as before this head; the liveness `RecordDetailView.tsx:1827` citation is :1848 on the merge head.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-vr8ygc`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzfhobWEgUUrjz4rrbh`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

Two must-fixes, both one-sitting: M1 the ADR-0035 (and ADR-0085 §2) amended status line for the default and the re-reading this head ships; M2 the `FIELD_GROUP_EMPTY` exemption for a `relatedList` group. The resolution function, the strict-name check, the `primary` re-reading and the inline-edit default are right against the card and the tree; the semver level and both declaration lines are right. The delta review closes M1, M2 and the seat's two asks (S3', S4) together.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

### ④ Design judgment

**packages/lint/src/validate-related-list-refs.ts + reference-integrity-suite.ts** — the door rule, tried against legitimate saves. It holds:

- *A stored sibling parent carries a dangling entry (its child was uninstalled, or it was saved under a closure) and the author saves an unrelated object or flow.* The finding is on another entry and identical in baseline and candidate (same `rule`, `where`, `path`, `message`; siblings keep their index across passes), so it cancels in the differential; the unrelated write is not refused.
- *The child's FK comes from an `objectExtension` (a sibling or downstream package extends the child, or extends a platform object such as a `sys_*` task with a lookup to the parent).* At the door the child row is the registry's folded view, so the FK is present and the parent's entry resolves; under a closure the fold has already happened before narrowing (narrowing drops rows, never fields), and a platform child survives limb 1. On the CLI `collectRelatedListNameErrors` merges the stack's and the package bodies' `objectExtensions`, pinned. Not refused.
- *Package closure.* A child in a downstream package that points in is outside the closure: unjudged, pinned. A child in the written package or a dependency is judged on its folded fields. A platform object with no FK to the parent is refused, which is what the reader does with it (places nothing).
- *The write is the child, and it drops the FK a stored parent names.* Accepted: the parent's finding reads the same with the child absent (baseline) as with it present without the FK (candidate), so it cancels. The parent's entry then dangles at runtime and the reader places nothing. This is the gate's located-on-another-entry policy, shared with every cross-object member, not a refusal; observation only.
- *A polymorphic or array `reference`, a `relatedList: false` FK, a self-reference, an entry spelled `object.field` against a child with one FK.* Each resolves exactly as `deriveRelatedLists` resolves it (string `reference` equal to the parent name; `false` is a relationship that exists and is hidden; a self FK is inbound; `object.field` matches that one FK).
- *`fields` in array form.* Not reachable: the written item has passed the object parse (`fields` is a record there) and registry rows are `ObjectSchema`-shaped.
- *`flow` writes.* The member runs, but `objects` is identical in both passes, so it can only cost time; no flow write can be refused by it.

No must-fix. The rule's docblock sentence "with the fields their `objectExtensions` add merged in" describes the CLI shape; at the door the merge is the registry's. Observation, not graded.
